name: The Mystery of the Third Planet

paragraphs.text: The Mystery of the Third Planet (, Tayna tretyey planety, also translated as The Secret of the Third Planet) is a 1981 Soviet traditionally animated feature film directed by Roman Kachanov and produced by the Soyuzmultfilm studio in Moscow. It is based on a 1964 novella by Kir Bulychev, part of the Alisa Seleznyova children's science fiction book series.

The movie is considered a cult classic in Russia and was included in various lists of the best animated films and science fiction films. A shortened novelization of The Mystery of the Third Planet was written by Bulychev himself, with other adaptations including a diafilm and a number of video games. The 2009 feature film Alice's Birthday is considered a spiritual successor of the work.

Retrospective reviews are positive. Kevin Lyons called it "Gloriously strange, it’s a richly animated tale full of offbeat details with characters who all have their own distinctive little quirks and idiosyncrasies”. Kali Wallace described the backgrounds as "particularly wonderful and whimsical" describing the film as a cult classic. While Kim Tibbs review at Click Clack concluded "If you’re looking for an animated movie that is as vibrant and imaginative as it is obscure, you can’t go wrong with The Mystery of the Third Planet.
